signals.signal: Targeted consultation on the review of MiCA (Reg (EU) 2023/1114), published 20/05/2026 under MiCA Arts.140 and 142, CLOSES 30/09/2026 23:59 CEST. Deadline was extended from 31/08/2026 (Commission Finance News Hub, 29/06/2026). Feeds a mandatory Commission report that may be accompanied by a legislative proposal amending MiCA.
signals.source_name: European Commission - Targeted consultation on the review of MiCA Regulation
signals.implies: Only ~5 weeks left for Printec and its bank customers to shape MiCA 2.0. Whatever emerges sets the compliance stack banks must buy for crypto/EMT services: AML/KYC (IMTF Siron, FICO), transaction monitoring (INETCO), eKYC onboarding (Namirial) and Thales HSM key custody.
signals.likelihood: Certain the consultation closes 30/09/2026; a legislative proposal in 2027 is likely but not confirmed
signals.followup: Read the consultation document (2026-mica-review-targeted-consultation-document_en.pdf) in full and extract questions touching custody, AML and CASP operational requirements; decide whether Printec responds via a trade body.

signals.entity: ESMA + all EU National Competent Authorities
signals.country: EU-wide (AT, BG, CY, CZ, GR, HR, HU, RO, SI, SK)
signals.signal: MiCA transitional period ENDED 1 JULY 2026 EU-wide. ESMA Public Statement ESMA75-113276571-1710 of 23/06/2026 orders unauthorised CASPs to wind down in an orderly manner: stop onboarding EU clients immediately, cease marketing, limit service to sale/transfer/close-out, keep full AML/CFT controls (CDD - customer due diligence, transaction monitoring, sanctions screening, STR reporting, travel-rule traceability) THROUGHOUT the wind-down, and communicate a hard auto-close deadline to clients. Where clients migrate to an authorised CASP, the receiving CASP must run full onboarding CDD. Builds on ESMA statement of 17/04/2026 (ESMA75-113276571-1679). NCAs may take coordinated action after the transitional period.
signals.source_name: ESMA Public Statement ESMA75-113276571-1710 (PDF, text extracted locally)
signals.implies: Two concrete demand pulses: (a) authorised CASPs and bank crypto arms must onboard migrating client books at volume - Namirial digital onboarding/eKYC; (b) both winding-down and receiving firms must run AML/CFT for the whole exit - IMTF Siron / FICO AML-KYC and INETCO transaction monitoring. Footprint reference base (Alpha Bank on Siron) is the natural entry point.
signals.likelihood: High over 6-12 months - client-book migration and enforcement are already under way
signals.followup: Pull the ESMA MiCA register and identify which authorised CASPs in AT/CY/CZ/GR/HR are absorbing client books; approach them and their banking partners on eKYC + AML.

signals.entity: Qivalis (Amsterdam JV) - incl. Raiffeisen Bank International (AT)
signals.signal: Qivalis, the bank-owned euro-stablecoin JV, has applied to De Nederlandsche Bank for an ELECTRONIC MONEY INSTITUTION licence so it can issue a MiCA e-money token (EMT - a crypto-asset referencing a single official currency, here the euro, redeemable 1:1). Raiffeisen Bank International is a named FOUNDING shareholder alongside BNP Paribas, ING, UniCredit, CaixaBank, BBVA, Danske, DekaBank, DZ Bank, KBC, SEB and Banca Sella. Consortium has since expanded to 37 banks across 15 countries. Launch targeted H2 2026, conditional on the DNB licence. Fireblocks supplies tokenisation, wallet and custody infrastructure. NOTE: membership counts and the H2-2026 launch window are PRESS-tier; the CaixaBank corporate newsroom item is the closest issuer-side confirmation.
signals.source_name: CaixaBank corporate newsroom - 'Qivalis, joint venture of a European banking consortium, to launch euro stablecoin in the second half of 2026'
signals.implies: RBI is a footprint bank with subsidiaries across CEE/SEE. A live bank-issued EMT forces distribution rails at RBI's network banks: wallet/custody key protection (Thales HSM/PCI), AML and travel-rule screening on token transfers (IMTF Siron, FICO), transaction monitoring (INETCO), and eKYC for wallet onboarding (Namirial). Raiffeisen Serbia is already an x-core customer - warm route in.
signals.likelihood: Medium-High that the DNB licence lands and distribution work starts in RBI CEE subsidiaries within 6-12 months
signals.followup: Confirm the DNB EMI authorisation against the DNB public register and RBI's own IR/press page; establish whether RBI plans distribution through its CEE subsidiaries and on what timetable.

signals.signal: CNB press release 'MiCA: CNB udelila kryptolicenci 11 subjektum' [MiCA: CNB has granted a crypto licence to 11 entities], 01/07/2026: CNB assessed 251 applications - THE HIGHEST NUMBER IN THE ENTIRE EU - and granted only 11 CASP authorisations (204 filed during the transitional period). CNB says many applications lacked essential information, came from entities with no trading history, virtual addresses or intent to operate abroad; only a small share showed transparent ownership and financing. First six licences were issued 11/02/2026. Board member Jan Prochazka framed MiCA as bringing clear rules and a higher protection standard. Unlicensed providers had to cease EU crypto services from 01/07/2026.
signals.implies: A 251-to-11 rejection rate says CNB is failing applicants on governance, AML and ICT controls - exactly the gaps Printec's compliance stack fills. Re-applicants and the 11 licensees both need audit-grade AML/KYC (IMTF Siron, FICO), transaction monitoring (INETCO) and eKYC (Namirial) before CNB will sign off. Czech banks using the Art.60 notification route face the same evidential bar.
signals.likelihood: High - a second application wave through 2026-2027 is near-certain given 240 unsuccessful filings
signals.followup: Get the CNB list of the 11 licensees from the Seznamy regulovanych subjektu; check whether any Czech credit institution (CSOB, Ceska sporitelna, Komercni banka) has filed an Art.60 notification.

signals.entity: Autoritatea de Supraveghere Financiara (ASF) / Government of Romania
signals.signal: Romania has NO designated MiCA competent authority. ASF stated (quoted 01/07/2026 and 05/07/2026) that it 'is not currently designated as competent authority for applying Regulation (EU) 2023/1114 (MiCA)' and therefore cannot receive or process authorisation requests. The draft emergency ordinance designating ASF had a first government reading on 02/04/2026 but stalled when the government fell on a no-confidence vote (late April/early May 2026); an interim government cannot issue emergency ordinances and Parliament was in recess until 01/09/2026. The European Commission has opened an INFRINGEMENT procedure against Romania. Meanwhile the MiCA transitional period expired 01/07/2026, leaving Romanian CASPs with no route to authorisation. PRESS-TIER: the ASF quote and the infringement step are reported by StartupCafe/Bursa/HotNews, not yet read off an ASF or Commission primary page.
signals.source_name: StartupCafe - 'Platformele crypto nu pot fi autorizate de ASF Romania... pentru ca nu avem lege interna' [Crypto platforms cannot be authorised by ASF Romania... because we have no domestic law]
signals.implies: Romania is a blocked market that must unblock fast. When Parliament returns 01/09/2026 and the designating act passes, a compressed authorisation wave follows - Romanian CASPs and BCR/BRD/Raiffeisen Romania Art.60 notifications will all need AML/KYC (IMTF Siron, FICO), transaction monitoring (INETCO) and eKYC (Namirial) evidence at once. BCR is already an NCR APTRA customer. Note BNR - not ASF - holds exclusive competence over EMT issuers.
signals.likelihood: High that the designating act moves in the Sept-Dec 2026 parliamentary session under infringement pressure
signals.followup: CLOSE THIS OUT: confirm the infringement procedure on the Commission's infringement decisions register, and watch Monitorul Oficial from 01/09/2026 for the designating OUG/law. Verify OUG 10/2025's actual scope - press reports conflict on whether it designated ASF at all.

signals.entity: Hrvatska agencija za nadzor financijskih usluga (HANFA)
signals.signal: HANFA news item 03/07/2026 'Pruzanje kriptousluga od 1. srpnja 2026.: za drustva obvezna kriptolicenca i upis u Hanfine registre, a korisnike se poziva na oprez' [Provision of crypto services from 1 July 2026: a crypto licence and entry in HANFA's registers are mandatory for firms, and users are urged to be cautious]. FIVE Croatian CASP licences granted; four already in the register - Bitblock, Digital Assets, Electrocoin and White Tech - with IN Kapital awaiting court registration. Electrocoin (Zagreb) was the first, licensed 09/04/2026. HANFA runs TWO registers: Croatian-licensed CASPs and notified EU firms. Credit institutions and investment firms already supervised by HANFA or the Hrvatska narodna banka go through a NOTIFICATION procedure (MiCA Art.60) rather than a full licence application.
signals.implies: Only five licensees for the whole Croatian market means the volume route is Art.60 bank notifications. Zagrebacka banka, PBZ, Erste&Steiermarkische and OTP Croatia each need the Art.60(7) evidence pack - programme of operations, internal control mechanisms, asset segregation, custody, AML and ICT - which maps directly to IMTF Siron / FICO AML-KYC, INETCO monitoring, Namirial eKYC and Thales HSM custody keys. Erste Croatia is already an APTRA OptiCash customer.
signals.likelihood: Medium over 6-12 months - Croatian bank Art.60 notifications are the plausible next wave
signals.followup: Open HANFA's notified-firms register and check whether any Croatian credit institution has filed an Art.60 notification; if none, that is the sales opening.

signals.signal: MNB granted Hungary's FIRST domestic MiCA CASP authorisation on 20/07/2026 to Tiwala Solutions Kft. (operator of CoinCash) - the only Hungarian-domiciled CASP under MiCA, with an unusually broad six-service permission, letting it passport into 27 markets. Hungarian law has required a MiCA authorisation for anyone providing crypto services in Hungary since 01/07/2025 (ahead of the EU transitional end). Bitpanda, Bybit, OKX, eToro and Crypto.com operate in Hungary on passported/MNB-recognised MiCA permissions. PRESS-TIER: date and scope come from Portfolio.hu, Vilaggazdasag and Economx (23-24/07/2026); not yet read off an MNB primary release.
signals.source_name: Portfolio.hu - 'Fordulat a hazai kriptopiacon: megszerezte a szukseges engedelyt' [Turning point in the domestic crypto market: it has obtained the necessary licence]
signals.implies: One domestic CASP for a 10m-population market leaves Hungarian banks (OTP, MBH, Erste Hungary, K&H, Raiffeisen Hungary) the Art.60 notification route if they want crypto custody/exchange. Each notification requires the same AML/ICT/custody evidence pack - IMTF Siron / FICO, INETCO, Namirial, Thales HSM. These are the same nine PSPs already carrying the 31/12/2026 rural-ATM mandate, so compliance budget is already open.
signals.followup: Verify the 20/07/2026 authorisation and its six service types against the MNB engedelyek/piaci szereplok register (mnb.hu); check for any Hungarian bank Art.60 notification.

signals.signal: Cyprus ran its own hard gate ahead of the EU date: CASPs registered under the Cyprus national regime had to lodge a COMPLETE MiCA authorisation application by 27/02/2026; those that filed in time could keep operating under the national regime until 01/07/2026 or until CySEC decided, whichever came first. From 01/07/2026 only a CySEC MiCA licence permits crypto services from a Cyprus base. CySEC keeps TWO registers - Art.63 authorised CASPs and Art.60 notifications by already-regulated financial firms. Revolut Digital Assets Europe (Limassol) holds CASP001/25, registered 20/10/2025. ACCESS PROBLEM: the CySEC CASP register page returned HTTP 410 Gone to the fetch tool, so the licensee count could not be read off the primary register.
signals.source_name: Harneys Regulatory Blog / Cyprus Mail 'Licence, logo or lookalike? Cyprus crypto changes under MiCA' (18/08/2026)
signals.implies: Cyprus is the footprint's densest CASP cluster, and the Art.60 register means Bank of Cyprus and Hellenic Bank can extend into crypto by notification. Both need the Art.60(7) pack: custody segregation, AML/CFT, ICT resilience - IMTF Siron / FICO, INETCO, Namirial eKYC, Thales HSM. Bank of Cyprus is an existing Printec customer (Glory TCR).
signals.followup: Re-fetch the CySEC CASP register with a desktop User-Agent (the /en-GB/entities/crypto-asset-services-providers-casps/ path 410s) and count Art.63 vs Art.60 entries; check specifically for Bank of Cyprus or Hellenic Bank on the Art.60 list.

signals.signal: The HCMC Board, at its 1096th meeting on 22/07/2026, granted GREECE'S FIRST TWO MiCA CASP authorisations: XENIOS BLOCKCHAIN GROUP A.E. (reception and transmission of orders in crypto-assets on behalf of clients) and CAPITAL WALLET GREECE MONOPROSOPI A.E. (custody and administration of crypto-assets on behalf of third parties). Greek-established firms wanting to provide crypto services now need an HCMC authorisation and, in some cases, Bank of Greece involvement. PRESS-TIER: reported by ot.gr, Powergame and Sofokleousin (22/07/2026); the HCMC board-decision page was not opened directly.
signals.source_name: Oikonomikos Tachydromos (ot.gr) - 'Epitropi Kefalaiagoras: dyo adeies leitourgias ypiresion kryptostoicheion' [HCMC: two crypto-asset service operating licences]
signals.implies: A licensed Greek CUSTODIAN is the significant part - custody means HSM-protected key management (Thales HSM/PCI) plus client-asset segregation controls and AML monitoring. Greek systemic banks (Alpha, NBG, Piraeus, Eurobank) now have a domestic precedent and the Art.60 notification route open. Alpha Bank already runs IMTF Siron for AML - the natural extension sale.
signals.likelihood: Medium-High that more Greek authorisations and at least one bank Art.60 notification follow within 6-12 months
signals.followup: Open the HCMC (hcmc.gr) board-decision announcement for meeting 1096 to move this to regulator tier, and monitor subsequent HCMC board meetings for further CASP licences and bank notifications.

signals.entity: Komisia za finansov nadzor (FSC/KFN) + Balgarska narodna banka (BNB)
signals.signal: FSC reminder 24/04/2026 'KFN pripomnya, che kriptofirmite tryabva da rabotyat s litsenz ot yuli' [FSC reminds that crypto firms must operate with a licence from July]: from 01/07/2026 any firm serving EU clients without a MiCA licence breaches EU law and must cease; unlicensed providers must have READY AND IMPLEMENTED orderly market-exit plans guaranteeing client protection, including transfer of assets to a licensed operator or a self-hosted wallet. Fines up to 15% of annual turnover. Only TWO Bulgarian firms are MiCA-licensed - Alaric Securities OOD (the first) and Belayer OOD; FSC REFUSED 4 of 8 applicants. Division of competence: FSC licenses and supervises CASPs; the BNB supervises E-MONEY TOKEN issuers.
signals.source_name: Investor.bg - 'KFN pripomnya, che kriptofirmite tryabva da rabotyat s litsenz ot yuli'
signals.implies: Bulgaria joins the euro on 01/01/2026, so BNB supervision of euro-denominated EMT issuance is now live, not theoretical - and a bank-distributed euro EMT would need BNB sign-off. A 50% refusal rate says the FSC bar is governance/AML/ICT evidence: IMTF Siron / FICO AML-KYC, INETCO transaction monitoring, Namirial eKYC. UniCredit Bulbank, DSK and Postbank are the Art.60 notification candidates.
signals.followup: Re-verify the licensee count and the 4-of-8 refusal figure against the FSC's own register at fsc.bg (regulated entities / CASP section); check whether the BNB has published any EMT-issuer guidance since euro adoption.

signals.signal: NBS press release 29/07/2026 'Kryptoaktiva po MiCA: Na Slovensku posobi sest licencovanych poskytovatelov, investicne riziko zostava' [Crypto-assets after MiCA: six licensed providers operate in Slovakia, investment risk remains]. SIX licensed CASPs in Slovakia; 312 entities EU-WIDE hold a CASP permission. MiCA has been applicable in Slovakia since 30/12/2025 - AHEAD of the 01/07/2026 EU-wide date. NBS warns that regulation raises provider safety and standards but 'does not eliminate investment risk, volatility, or fraudulent offers'. NBS survey: 88.5% of Slovaks have heard of crypto, 13.4% have practical experience.
signals.implies: 312 authorised CASPs for the whole EU is a very small regulated perimeter - it confirms the addressable compliance market is concentrated and that banks taking the Art.60 route will be a large share of future growth. NBS's consumer-protection framing signals supervisory focus on conduct and fraud, which is INETCO transaction-monitoring and FICO fraud-analytics territory. Slovak banks (Slovenska sporitelna, VUB, Tatra banka) are the Art.60 candidates.
signals.followup: Pull the NBS list of the six licensees from nbs.sk/dohlad-nad-financnym-trhom/.../kryptoaktiva/; track the EU-wide 312 figure against the ESMA register as the market-sizing denominator.

signals.signal: MiCA has consolidated the Slovenian market hard: of roughly 35 domestic crypto providers, only THREE now hold an ATVP MiCA CASP licence - Ilirika, Incrementum and Orcabay - while about 24 providers (mostly large passported platforms: Bitpanda, Bitstamp, Coinbase, Crypto.com, eToro, Gemini, Kraken, Robinhood, Trade Republic) may serve Slovenian clients. Ilirika, a brokerage house, took Slovenia's FIRST ATVP MiCA licence on 26/09/2025 (custody, order execution, reception and transmission of orders, portfolio management). Slovenia ran a SHORT six-month transitional period ending July 2025, well ahead of the EU date. ACCESS: atvp.si returned HTTP 403 to both the fetch tool and a desktop-User-Agent curl (Cloudflare JS interstitial), and the Delo article 302-redirected to an error page, so the 35-to-3 figure is press-tier and unverified against the ATVP register.
signals.source_name: Delo - 'Uredba MiCA zdesetkala slovenske kriptoponudnike' [The MiCA Regulation has decimated Slovenian crypto providers] / Bloomberg Adria (first licence)
signals.implies: Slovenia shows the pattern that matters commercially: the survivors are REGULATED FINANCIAL FIRMS (a brokerage took the first licence), not native crypto shops - because they already had the governance, AML and ICT evidence base. That is the argument for selling the Art.60 evidence pack to NLB, NKBM and Intesa Sanpaolo Slovenia: IMTF Siron / FICO, INETCO, Namirial, Thales HSM.
signals.followup: OPERATOR TASK: retrieve the ATVP CASP register (atvp.si) through a real browser and confirm the licensee count and names; the site defeats both scripted routes.

signals.entity: Verkhovna Rada of Ukraine / Association of Ukrainian Banks (AUB) / NBU
signals.signal: Ukraine's virtual-assets framework, DRAFT LAW No.10225-d, is explicitly BASED ON MiCA and adapted to Ukrainian conditions. It was adopted in FIRST READING on 03/09/2025 (246 votes) and is still being prepared for second reading as at 13/08/2026. The Association of Ukrainian Banks states (13/08/2026) that the framework 'will allow banks and financial companies to officially and legally work with virtual assets', naming three bank use cases: stablecoins for cheaper/faster cross-border payments, digital-asset management for customers through their own bank, and digital assets as LOAN COLLATERAL. The Ukrainian model adds civil-law provisions, restrictions on virtual assets as a means of payment, and martial-law adaptations. Tax Code amendments (5% preferential PIT for 2026 on pre-existing holdings, 18% plus military levy thereafter) are tied to 01/01/2026. It is still NOT settled whether the NBU or the NSSMC will be the crypto-market regulator. NO adopted law and NO firm second-reading date exists - treat every downstream date as unconfirmed.
signals.source_name: Association of Ukrainian Banks - 'Virtual Assets for Banks: From Stablecoins to New Financial Products'
signals.implies: If 10225-d passes, Ukrainian banks get a legal route into custody, stablecoin payments and crypto-collateralised lending in one step - and each needs AML/KYC (IMTF Siron, FICO), transaction monitoring (INETCO), eKYC (Namirial) and HSM key custody (Thales). PrivatBank is an existing Printec NCR-recycler customer and the obvious first conversation. This stacks on NBU Board Resolution No.143 (information-security requirements, biting 13/12/2026), so the security budget is already open.
signals.likelihood: Medium - second reading has slipped repeatedly since Sept-2025; passage within 6-12 months is plausible but unconfirmed
signals.followup: Track draft law 10225-d on the Rada's own legislative register (w1.c1.rada.gov.ua) for a second-reading date and the final choice of regulator (NBU vs NSSMC); check bank.gov.ua with a desktop User-Agent for any NBU virtual-asset position paper.

signals.entity: Governments of North Macedonia and Montenegro
signals.signal: Both non-EU footprint markets have signalled MiCA-aligned crypto licensing regimes for 2026 but NEITHER has adopted one. North Macedonia has announced plans to introduce a VASP/exchange licensing regime during 2026, expected to be closely aligned with MiCA, with draft laws and amendments during 2026, then secondary regulation and supervisory guidance, and first licences possibly in 2026 subject to parliamentary adoption. Montenegro: PM Spajic announced in September 2025 that a MiCA-conforming law would soon be adopted and the Ministry of Finance launched a public consultation on draft legislation; authorities have signalled they want to finalise virtual-asset legislation in 2026. Montenegro's Parliament did adopt AML/CFT amendments in February 2025 defining crypto-assets and the associated services. NO adopted text, NO gazette citation and NO firm date was found for either - these are announced intentions only. [STANDING - dated 2025/2026 announcements]
signals.source_name: CEE Legal Matters - 'North Macedonia: A Path Toward Regulating Crypto Markets' / Crypto for Innovation - 'Montenegro Takes Tentative Steps Towards Crypto Regulation'
signals.implies: Watch-only for now. If either adopts a MiCA mirror, the first-wave licensees will need the same AML/KYC and ICT evidence base (IMTF Siron, FICO, INETCO, Namirial) and the local banks will face Art.60-equivalent notification questions. MK already carries the 30/09/2026 single-register-of-accounts obligation, so the regulator has a crowded 2026.
signals.likelihood: Low-Medium within 6-12 months - both are announcements without adopted text
signals.followup: Check the Sluzben vesnik na RSM and the Sluzbeni list Crne Gore, plus the NBRNM (nbrm.mk, desktop User-Agent) and CBCG news pages, for an actual draft or adopted crypto-asset law. Bosnia & Herzegovina and Kosovo surfaced NOTHING this run - re-sweep next run.

signals.entity: European Systemic Risk Board (ESRB) / European Commission
signals.signal: The substantive fight inside the MiCA review is THIRD-COUNTRY MULTI-ISSUANCE - stablecoins issued jointly by an EU entity and a non-EU entity and designed to be FUNGIBLE, so a holder can redeem the same token from either issuer. The ESRB General Board adopted Recommendation ESRB/2025/9 on third-country multi-issuer stablecoin schemes (recommendation dated 25/09/2025, published 20/10/2025), warning that a run could push holders to redeem from the EU issuer and strain its reserves, and that third-country restrictions on reserve transfers would worsen it. The ESRB's core finding is that MiCA 'does not explicitly envisage' joint EU/third-country issuance and therefore cannot address the risk; a Council working document reportedly argues MiCA 'lacks dedicated tools' for the multi-issuer model. This is a live question in the 30/09/2026 consultation. [STANDING - Recommendation dated 2025; the live trigger is the 30/09/2026 consultation close]
signals.source_name: ESRB - Recommendation of the European Systemic Risk Board of 25 September 2025 (ESRB/2025/9) + ESRB press release
signals.implies: Indirect but real for Printec: if MiCA 2.0 tightens reserve-segregation and redemption rules, EMT issuers (including a bank consortium like Qivalis with RBI inside it) will need auditable reserve-attestation, redemption-flow monitoring and segregation controls - INETCO transaction monitoring plus Thales HSM for reserve/redemption key control. MiCA already requires at least 30% of EMT reserves to sit as deposits with separate credit institutions, which makes footprint banks candidate reserve-deposit takers and brings the controls in-house.
signals.likelihood: High that multi-issuance is addressed in the Commission's post-consultation report; legislative change is 2027+
signals.followup: Read ESRB/2025/9 in full and cross-reference its recommendations against the consultation questionnaire; verify the 30% reserve-deposit requirement directly against MiCA Art.54/Title IV rather than secondary commentary.

coverage_notes: Fresh full run - no checkpoint existed for 27/08/2026. Angles used: (1) EU-level primary - Commission consultation page, ESMA public statements (PDF text extracted locally with pdftotext), EBA MiCA pages, ESRB recommendation; (2) national-regulator local-language sweep in Czech, Slovak, Hungarian, Croatian, Slovenian, Bulgarian, Greek, Romanian, German and Serbian, plus Ukrainian - CNB, NBS-SK, HANFA, ATVP, FSC/BNB, HCMC, ASF/BNR, FMA, MNB, NBS-RS; (3) bank-side primary/issuer sources for the Qivalis EMT (CaixaBank newsroom) and Ukrainian banks (AUB). REGULATOR-TIER PRIMARIES OPENED: ESMA75-113276571-1710 (23/06/2026), CNB press release (01/07/2026), NBS-SK press release (29/07/2026), HANFA news (03/07/2026), European Commission consultation page (20/05/2026). GENUINE GAPS: (a) Bosnia & Herzegovina and Kosovo produced NO crypto-asset regulatory development at all this run - neither has a MiCA-mirror in train that surfaced; (b) no footprint bank was found to have filed a MiCA Art.60 notification - the registers that would prove it (CySEC, HANFA notified-firms, CNB, MNB) were not all opened, so 'no bank has notified' is UNPROVEN, not established; (c) the ESMA MiCA register itself was not enumerated, so per-country licensee counts rest on each NCA's own statement; (d) no bank-issued EMT other than Qivalis was found touching the footprint. DELIBERATELY NOT RE-REPORTED (baseline, unchanged): the 30/09/2026 consultation close was already in the baseline calendar - it is retained here only because the legal basis (MiCA Arts.140 & 142), the 20/05/2026 publication date and the 29/06/2026 extension from 31/08/2026 are NEW detail the baseline did not carry. CROSS-WORKSTREAM NOTE: the Romanian MiCA infringement and the 01/09/2026 parliamentary return are relevant to whoever holds the Romania beat. PRINTEC MAPPING is consistent across signals: MiCA Art.60(7) and Art.63 both demand a programme of operations, internal control mechanisms, asset segregation, custody, AML/CFT and ICT evidence - IMTF Siron / FICO (AML-KYC), INETCO (transaction monitoring), Namirial (digital onboarding/eKYC), Thales HSM/PCI (custody and reserve key protection). No Printec hardware line (ATM, TCR, POS) is directly triggered by MiCA; the crypto-ATM angle was searched and produced no footprint-specific regulator action, only a French AMF precedent. NO VERIFICATION DEBT from the carried list falls in this workstream - all seven carried debts (CY EAA, CY VoP, AT/HR EUDI, DORA subcontracting RTS, HU ATM decree, BG instant-payments basis, UA banknote) belong to other workstreams. CONFIDENCE: capped at Medium per the single-agent rule; press-tier-only items (Qivalis membership/launch window, HU and GR licence dates, BG counts, SI counts, UA and WB legislative status) are marked Low or flagged in-line.
